summary: Skills unified onto one source tree with a gated contract (ADR 0013). They had accumulated in two places — .claude/skills held add-component and review-ui, registry/skills held ui-craft — with no shared standard and no gate on either. They are not duplicates: one tier teaches an agent to build this library, the other to use it in a consumer's app. But a split audience does not need a split source, and having one made the standard impossible to state. registry/skills is now the source of truth for BOTH tiers, applying the rule the repo already holds — the manifest, not the folder, is the distribution boundary, which is why stories and tests already live under registry/ without shipping. .claude/skills becomes generated output: committed and staleness-gated like registry.json, written byte-identical to source so the copy this repo loads is the copy a consumer installs, with the do-not-edit warning in a generated README rather than inside the files. skill is now a first-class manifest type emitting registry:file, so the checker finds skills by type instead of guessing at paths. check:skills validates front matter, the per-tier naming rule (product skills carry the diorama- namespace because they land in a consumer's shared .claude/skills), install targets, and generated freshness; all three rules probed by breaking them. The description rules are the substantive ones — 80-character floor, 900 ceiling, required trigger clause — because a skill loads on its description ALONE and a bad one fails silently, which is the only failure class these gates exist to convert into noise. Adds the create-skill skill, so the standard is documented as a skill rather than as prose about skills, and makes this repo dogfood diorama-ui-craft at the exact path consumers install it to.

migration.manual: Skills moved from .claude/skills/<name>/ to registry/skills/<name>/. Edit the source there and run `pnpm skills:build`; edits made directly in .claude/skills are discarded on the next build and reported by `pnpm check:skills`. The ui-craft manifest item changes type from "file" to "skill" — the generated registry output is unchanged, since skill emits registry:file.
